_comment: PRD §7 'Initial policies/perks'. §7 lists five and then says: 'For MVP, either omit policies or include only two to reduce balance complexity.' These are the two — House Special and Friendly Staff — reproduced with §7's own effect prose and intended strategy. Express Service, Lean Operations and Premium Experience are deliberately absent; adding them is a balance change, not a data entry. `effects` is machine-readable in the same style as upgrades.json: every key is a value a system reads, multipliers are 1.0-relative. `requiresMenuDish` marks a policy whose effect names a dish — House Special is 'ONE TAGGED DISH gets increased appeal', so the submission must say which, and setup-validator.js rejects a target that is not on the submitted menu. Nothing consumes `effects` yet: the customer-choice and satisfaction systems that will are STORY-004 and STORY-012.

policies.name: House Special
policies.description: One dish on your menu is the house special: higher appeal and higher satisfaction.

policies.name: Friendly Staff
policies.description: Satisfaction decays more slowly while guests are waiting.
